statement: A raft follower that detects a same-index term conflict at or below its committed index stops retrying an impossible truncation and instead surfaces the poisoned committed prefix to the existing snapshot/forced-repair path exactly once: truncateConflictingSameIndexTail (src/raft/liferaft.js) currently trusts the per-entry committed flag while sqlite-log-adapter.removeEntriesAfter refuses by committed index, so when base commit-index catch-up has already advanced over a stale same-index entry (the CL-040 hazard) every subsequent leader heartbeat re-requests a truncation the adapter must refuse — an unbounded livelock that starves formation. Verified at HEAD 08acaf0d8 across 19 archived 3-node runs: every heavy-refusal run (46-363 'Refused raft log truncation into the committed prefix' retries) failed formation with joiners stuck in joining:readiness-convergence, while green runs show 0-6 transient refusals; the wedge is the dominant face of the current ~50% boot flake (5 of ~8 genuine reds). The fix must be fail-closed: a committed-prefix term conflict is committed-state divergence and must trigger typed divergence surfacing plus the existing repair/catch-up route, never a silent skip that leaves divergent committed state, and never a weakening of the committed-entry-loss refusal in the log adapter.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
